morningSnapshot.headline: Bank of Canada Holds Rate at 2¼%; Ottawa Pauses Fuel Tax as Tariff Pressures Mount
morningSnapshot.summary: The Bank of Canada keeps its policy rate steady at 2.25% while Ottawa extends the pause on the federal fuel excise tax. Meanwhile, FedDev Ontario rolls out over $12.5 million in support for Hamilton-area businesses weathering U.S. tariffs.

topStory.headline: Bank of Canada maintains the policy rate at 2¼%
topStory.summary: The Bank of Canada held its target for the overnight rate at 2.25%, keeping the Bank Rate at 2.5% and the deposit rate at 2.20%.
topStory.whyItMatters: For homeowners with a 5-year variable mortgage like yours, a steady policy rate provides immediate stability on borrowing costs following previous adjustments.
topStory.explainMore:
The Bank of Canada announced today that it is holding its target for the overnight rate at 2.25%. Alongside this decision, the Bank Rate is maintained at 2.5% and the deposit rate sits at 2.20%.

Governor Tiff Macklem discussed key factors in the Governing Council’s deliberations during the accompanying monetary policy decision press conference opening statement, weighing economic momentum against ongoing domestic and international pressures.

This decision arrives on the heels of recent national accounts data showing real gross domestic product increased 0.8% in the second quarter of 2026, driven by exports, household spending, and business capital investment.

stories.headline: Nine Hamilton businesses receive Government of Canada support to strengthen Canadian supply chains and drive growth
stories.summary: FedDev Ontario announced a combined repayable investment of over $12.5 million to help nine Hamilton-area businesses respond to tariff-related pressures, strengthen domestic supply chains, and position themselves for long-term growth.
stories.whyItMatters: Operating in the regional industrial corridor near Hamilton, local manufacturing supply chains face direct cross-border trade headwinds and tariff pressures.
stories.explainMore:
Minister of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Innovation Evan Solomon announced the federal funding package aimed at bolstering regional supply chains.

The investment is specifically structured to help industrial businesses in the Hamilton area adapt to tariff-related pressures and secure long-term operational resilience.

Federal officials, including Minister Mélanie Joly and Minister Rechie Valdez, have also highlighted broader federal support measures geared toward protecting Canadian workers and businesses navigating ongoing U.S. trade disruptions.

stories.headline: Ottawa set to extend the pause on federal fuel excise tax: source
stories.summary: A planned renewal of the federal excise tax on fuel that was to kick in after Labour Day will be paused, according to a government source ahead of the finance minister's afternoon announcement.
stories.whyItMatters: Extending the fuel tax pause offers temporary relief on transportation and fuel costs as living expenses remain a central pressure for consumers.
stories.explainMore:
The federal government is moving to extend the suspension of the fuel excise tax, which was originally scheduled to snap back into place following the Labour Day long weekend.

This extension comes as convenience store chains like Couche-Tard report that consumers are cutting back on discretionary items like snacks due to rising living and fuel costs.

Finance officials are set to detail the mechanics of the continued tax pause.

markets.insight: North American equities retreated on Tuesday with the TSX down 0.97% to 53.13 and the S&P 500 slipping 0.69% to 761.78. Oil jumped 5.46% to $141, while the Canadian dollar held steady at 0.7208 USD.

yourMoney.headline: Bank of Canada Holds Policy Rate at 2¼%
yourMoney.summary: The Bank of Canada maintained its target for the overnight rate at 2.25%, keeping borrowing conditions stable for variable-rate mortgage holders.
yourMoney.whyItMatters: With your 5-year variable mortgage tied directly to policy rate decisions, today's hold avoids any sudden payment hikes while economic growth registers a modest 0.8% increase in Q2 2026.

manufacturing.headline: FedDev Ontario Deploys $12.5M to Shield Hamilton Supply Chains from Tariffs
manufacturing.summary: Federal investments target regional industrial resilience as Ministers Joly and Valdez highlight ongoing federal programs to support businesses grappling with U.S. trade barriers.
manufacturing.whyItMatters: Regional manufacturers in the Hamilton and Niagara industrial orbit face direct cost pressures from U.S. tariffs, making supply chain reinforcement and capital backing critical for long-term operational stability.
manufacturing.engineeringHeadline: Ontario Industrial Supply Chains Adapt to U.S. Trade Friction
manufacturing.engineeringSummary: While industrial hubs like Sudbury navigate critical mineral trade disputes without panic, southern Ontario manufacturing facilities are leveraging federal funding programs to strengthen domestic supply chains, automate operations, and mitigate cross-border tariff impacts.

world.headline: Nepal Flood Death Toll Exceeds 900 as Rescue Operations Continue
world.summary: Disaster response agencies report mounting casualties and hundreds still missing following catastrophic glacier collapse and flooding in the Himalayan border region.
world.whyItMatters: The disaster has disrupted vital infrastructure, including hydropower facilities where workers remain trapped, and prompted Canadian Nepalese communities to cancel traditional Teej festivals.
